clue.text: Rows in forms that will please the eye

definitions.note: a phrase for a quality that is attractive to look at, standing for the noun

indicators.note: in tells us the rows go inside the forms, so one word is placed within the other

parts.note: forms means shapes
rows means lines

explanation.surface: Rows of beds laid out in pleasing patterns for a garden designer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rows' looks like quarrels or oarsmen, but means lines; the definition is a phrase standing for a quality, so the noun fits it.
explanation.definitionFit: Shapeliness is an attractive outline or figure, a quality that pleases anyone looking at it.

clue.text: Order to troops to prepare for action — reason may follow

definitions.text: Order to troops to prepare for action — reason may follow

parts.words: Order to troops to prepare for action — reason may follow
parts.note: a military command telling soldiers to get ready, which with the word reason after it makes a phrase meaning 'is logical'

explanation.surface: A sergeant barks a command, and explanations may come later.
explanation.walkthrough: The command is followed by 'reason' to give the idiom 'stand to reason', meaning to be obviously logical.
explanation.definitionFit: Stand to is the military command for soldiers to take up positions ready for an attack.

clue.text: A brief, for example, is for the defence

parts.note: the brief or shortened form of 'for example' is e.g.
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lawyer's brief is one example of material used in a defence case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' looks like a lawyer's brief, but it signals the abbreviation of 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aegis means protection or sponsorship, from the shield of Zeus, so it is a kind of defence.

clue.text: This military order looks fine

parts.note: looks as a verb means eyes
fine, as in 'all right', means right

explanation.surface: A parade command that looks just the job.
explanation.definitionFit: On parade, the command eyes right tells soldiers to turn their heads to salute a dignitary.

clue.text: Inordinately vain man who had a terrible reputation

definitions.text: man who had a terrible reputation

indicators.note: inordinately suggests something out of all order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An excessively conceited man was notorious for his cruelty.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan the Terrible was the sixteenth-century Russian tsar, famous for his brutal rule.

clue.text: A pilot's emergency exit

parts.note: the way a fighter pilot leaves a doomed aircraft, by being shot out in a seat

explanation.surface: How an airman bails out when something goes badly wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Ejection is the act of being thrown out, here by an ejector seat from a cockpit.

clue.text: Someone mending a pipe

definitions.meaning: a person who stitches clothes, one who sews
a drainage channel carrying waste water underground

explanation.surface: A plumber is mending a broken pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are pronounced differently: one rhymes with 'lower', the other with 'fewer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Read one way the word is a needleworker; read the other it is a drain for waste.

clue.text: Birds give strange shrieks

indicators.note: strange means odd or out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Some birds make weird screaming noises.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrikes are songbirds, the butcher-birds that impale their prey on thorns.

clue.text: A particular form of dislike

parts.note: a particular form or variant of something is a version

explanation.surface: One specific kind of distaste.
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a strong feeling of dislike for something.

clue.text: Collect material for concrete

definitions.meaning: to gather together into one mass or total
the gravel and crushed stone mixed with cement to make concrete

explanation.surface: Gather up the ingredients needed to make concrete.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means gather into a whole; as a noun it is the stony filler in concrete.

clue.text: Hesitate to declare after Warwickshire's opening

indicators.note: after tells us the word for declare comes behind the county's first letter
the opening of a word is its first letter, taken from the county name

parts.note: to declare means to aver, to state firmly

explanation.surface: A cricket captain dithers over declaring once Warwickshire's innings has begun.
explanation.walkthrough: Warwickshire is an English county with a well-known cricket team; to declare in cricket is to end an innings early.
explanation.definitionFit: To waver is to be undecided, to hesitate between choices.

clue.text: Run out on the sand

definitions.meaning: to abandon someone, leaving them in the lurch
a dry sandy wasteland such as the Sahara

explanation.surface: A cricketer is run out on a sandy beach pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means abandon; as a noun it is an arid, sandy region.

clue.text: Sci-fi show celebrity to take long, hard journey

parts.note: a celebrity is a star
to trek is to make a long arduous journey

explanation.surface: A famous person has to slog a long way for a science-fiction programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Star Trek is the long-running American science-fiction television series.

clue.text: Love to wander about a royal house

parts.note: love is a zero score in tennis, the letter O
to range is to roam or wander about

explanation.surface: A romantic urge to roam around a palace.
explanation.definitionFit: The House of Orange is the Dutch royal dynasty, which also supplied Britain's William III.

clue.text: No one is missing full board and lodging

definitions.meaning: everyone has been located and accounted for
an old term for a servant's wages that included food and a room

explanation.surface: A hotel offering full board reports that no guests have gone astray.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is a dated British phrase used in job advertisements for servants, meaning everything provided.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both everybody located and, in old wage terms, all keep supplied as well as pay.

clue.text: They form some unit of the Canadian police

indicators.note: to form here means to make up into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: They make up a certain unit within Canada's police force.
explanation.definitionFit: Mounties is the familiar name for the Royal Canadian Mounted Police officers.

clue.text: Dive for weapon to use after dark?

parts.note: after dark means at night
a club is a heavy stick used as a weapon

explanation.surface: Reaching for a cosh to use when the sun has gone down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dive' looks like a verb but is the noun for a seedy bar or club.
explanation.definitionFit: A dive is slang for a disreputable drinking place or club open late.

clue.text: American state banks are, after the crunch

indicators.note: a crunch crushes and scrambles, so the letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: An American state's banks are in trouble after the credit crunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebraska is a Midwestern state of the USA.

clue.text: When away from land everyone is completely disorganised

parts.note: everyone means all
when a ship is away from land it is at sea

explanation.surface: On a voyage the whole crew is in total chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: To be all at sea is an idiom for being confused and bewildered.

clue.text: The defendant also made charges

definitions.meaning: the person on trial in a court
brought a charge against someone, past tense

explanation.surface: The person on trial also brought allegations of their own.
explanation.definitionFit: The accused is the defendant in a trial; to have accused is to have made charges.

clue.text: Drink triple gin, initially, with one rum

indicators.note: rum here is the adjective meaning odd, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the initial letter of gin, G, taken three times

explanation.surface: Someone orders three gins and a rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like another spirit but is the anagram signal, rearranging GGG with ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggnog is a drink of beaten eggs, milk and sugar, often laced with spirits.

clue.text: General disorder, one gathers

indicators.note: disorder means mess, so the word's letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A general's confusion, one gathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one gathers' reads like 'it seems', but it defines a person who gathers.
explanation.definitionFit: A gleaner is someone who gathers leftover grain or information bit by bit.

clue.text: Note garden feature in China

parts.note: C is a musical note
a rockery is a garden bed built of stones and plants

explanation.surface: A remark about a garden feature seen in China.
explanation.definitionFit: China in the sense of porcelain tableware is crockery.

clue.text: They're up for the celebration

parts.note: a jolly party is a ...-up, so the body parts raised are the ones in that phrase

explanation.surface: Guests are keen to come to the party.
explanation.walkthrough: A knees-up is British slang for a lively party.
explanation.definitionFit: The joints raised in dancing give the British slang word for a party.

clue.text: Bring the match alive with shot at goal

definitions.meaning: to light a match by rubbing it
a kick or shot aimed at the goal in football

explanation.surface: A striker livens up the football game with an attempt to score.
explanation.definitionFit: To strike a match sets it alight, and a striker's shot at goal is also called a strike.

clue.text: Part of a book gets Enid upset and cross

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the name's letters are jumbled

parts.note: a cross is the letter X

explanation.surface: Enid gets annoyed and angry with part of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' and 'cross' look like moods, but 'upset' rearranges ENID to INDE and 'cross' is X.
explanation.definitionFit: The index is the alphabetical list at the back of a book.

clue.text: This man gets a seat

parts.note: a German man's name which, with the word man added, makes a padded footstool or seat

explanation.surface: A gentleman is offered a chair.
explanation.walkthrough: Add MAN to the name to get OTTOMAN, a low upholstered seat.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is a man's, and joined with a following word it forms a kind of seat.

clue.text: One of five, one may feel

definitions.meaning: sight, hearing, taste, smell or touch

explanation.surface: Touch is one of the five faculties a person feels with.
explanation.definitionFit: There are five senses, and a sense is also a feeling or awareness someone has.

clue.text: Became comfortably established in seat on row

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the word for row follows the seat

parts.note: a settle is a high-backed wooden bench
row, rhyming with cow, means a din

explanation.surface: Someone got comfortable in a seat on a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' reads as a line of seats but means a noisy din.
explanation.definitionFit: To have settled in is to have become used to new surroundings.

clue.text: Dog goes after dog, but he won't fight seriously

indicators.note: goes after places the first dog word behind the second

parts.note: to dog someone is to shadow them
a boxer is a breed of dog

explanation.surface: One dog chases another, but neither fights for real.
explanation.definitionFit: A shadow-boxer spars against an imaginary opponent for practice, not a real bout.
